title: Cache pose topology decisions in SkeletonSnapshot
description:
## Summary
The indexed skeleton foundation removed repeated hierarchy scans, but `PoseRotationResolver.ResolveIntoCompatible` still recomputes semantic child-selection decisions every pose application. It loops the children of each bone to rediscover the continuation child for segmented bones and the primary child for non-segment bones. Cache these stable topology decisions at snapshot-capture time so the steady-state pose path is purely indexed.

## Scope
- Add explicit snapshot-owned indices for a segmented bone's continuation child and for any non-segment primary child needed by pose rotation.
- Derive them once using the same deterministic rules currently implemented (`SourcePartId` preference/endpoint matching and deterministic ID selection).
- Validate ambiguity and missing continuation metadata at capture/build time; do not silently select a different child per frame.
- Update `PoseRotationResolver` to consume cached indices with no per-frame child traversal or string comparison.
- Preserve the current behavior and existing deterministic bent-chain/attachment-branch tests.
- Consider the cached choice part of skeleton compatibility so two snapshots cannot differ only in pose-topology metadata while passing compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Steady-state `CreatureRig.ApplyPose` performs no child-list iteration, semantic string comparison, or per-bone topology discovery.
- Existing continuation-child and primary-child selection outputs remain identical for valid snapshots.
- Branching skeletons retain deterministic behavior independent of authored child insertion order.
- Snapshot capture rejects structurally ambiguous continuation metadata rather than deferring the failure to animation frames.
- Focused benchmarks show the cached path scales with bone count and not with repeated child-search work.

## Validation
- Runtime tests for straight chains, bent two/three-segment chains, branch-plus-attachment cases, terminals, and ambiguous topology.
- Repeated `ApplyPose` allocation test remains zero managed allocations after warmup.
- A focused microbenchmark or repeated-call measurement demonstrates that no topology discovery occurs per call.
- PlayMode confirmation on a generated creature covers a bent segmented chain and attachment branch.

## Findings
This is a second-order performance finding, not a reopening of the fixed continuation-child correctness bug. `SkeletonSnapshot.GetChildren(i)` is already O(1), but `PoseRotationResolver` still loops those children on every call to rediscover a stable relationship. The same pattern appears in the snapshot philosophy generally: stable structural facts should be resolved once at the immutable boundary and consumed by index thereafter.

## Blockers
Coordinate with TSK-0118 and TSK-0200 so the cached topology and final animation-pose representation share one compatibility contract.

## Next Step
Add the cached child indices to `SkeletonSnapshot`, port the resolver, and compare current-versus-cached pose outputs over the existing regression matrix.

comments.body: Created from peer review of the current PoseRotationResolver. Earlier audits correctly celebrated precomputed child lists, but the resolver still scans children to choose continuation/primary relationships on every frame. This task preserves those deterministic rules while moving the decision to immutable snapshot capture.
